headline: Created a White House commission on religious liberty
why: An advisory commission with no regulatory power; a Democratic president could keep it or let it lapse without a fight.

headline: Cut off federal funding for risky gain-of-function virus research
why: A research-safety funding restriction that most administrations of either party would keep, resting on grant policy rather than law.

headline: Sped up FDA and EPA approvals for factories making critical medicines
why: Domestic drug manufacturing is a goal both parties share, and the order only directs agencies to move faster under existing law.

headline: Told agencies to limit criminal penalties for breaking federal regulations
how: Restore criminal enforcement of federal rules.
why: It asks agencies to publish guidance on regulatory crimes, a criminal-justice reform goal many Democrats share; it changes no statute.

headline: Ordered the Federal Register to publish faster and review agency fees
why: Housekeeping: it orders reports on publication times and a fee review, with no effect on anyone's rights.

headline: Created a veterans housing center on the West Los Angeles VA campus
why: A veterans' housing project set up inside the VA by order; a Democratic president would keep it.

headline: Ordered officials to push U.S. drug prices down to the lowest paid abroad
why: A drug-price goal a Democratic president would keep; the pharma trade deals struck under it are separate rows.

headline: Cut the reciprocal tariff on China from 125 to 10 percent for 90 days
why: It lowered a tariff, and the Supreme Court has since voided all of the emergency-powers tariffs, so there is nothing to undo.

headline: Cleared the way for new nuclear reactors on military and energy sites
why: It directs agencies to host reactors on federal land under existing law; clean power for data centers is not something to reverse.

headline: Ordered a rewrite of nuclear safety rules with 18-month licensing deadlines
why: The rewrite is due in November 2026, so by 2029 it will sit in final rules, and changing those takes a new rulemaking.

headline: Told the Energy Department to speed reactor testing
why: A testing-speed directive inside one department; a Democratic president could keep the goal and tighten the safety review instead.

headline: Set a goal of 10 large nuclear reactors under construction by 2030
why: A goal for the nuclear supply chain with no new legal power attached; both parties back more nuclear.

headline: Put political appointees in charge of agency scientific integrity
why: It sets rules for how agencies use science by presidential direction, with no statute behind it.

headline: Directed the FAA to lift the ban on supersonic flight over land
why: A transportation rule change the FAA can make or reverse; nothing here harms a person or a program.

headline: Gave agencies new powers to track and bring down unauthorized drones
why: A counter-drone security directive that a Democratic president would likely keep; it sets task forces and plans, not new law.

headline: Cut back Biden's cybersecurity order, dropping its software security mandates
why: It amends an earlier executive order, so a new order can restore what it struck; no rule or statute sits underneath.

headline: Ordered faster drone approvals and more U.S. drone production
why: An industrial and aviation-policy push that a Democratic president would likely keep, with no new legal power attached.

headline: Ordered federal wildfire programs merged and fire-related rules reviewed
why: It directs the Interior and Agriculture departments to coordinate, so one signature changes it, but better firefighting coordination is not a harm to reverse.

headline: Set terms of the U.S.-UK trade deal, with lower tariffs on UK cars
why: The trade deal terms stand; its emergency-powers tariff piece fell with the Court's ruling, while car and steel terms rest on other law.

headline: Delayed the TikTok ban another 90 days
why: The ban comes from a statute; the order only delays enforcement, and a delay harms no one.

headline: Created a White House office for special peace missions
why: A staff office inside the White House; any president can reshape or rename it at will.

headline: Lifted U.S. economic sanctions on Syria
why: Ending sanctions after Assad's fall is policy most of Washington backed; a later president could reimpose targeted sanctions by order.

headline: Created a White House commission on outdoor recreation and conservation
why: An advisory commission with no regulatory power.

headline: Raised national park entry fees for foreign visitors
why: A fee policy set under existing park authority; it does not touch American visitors or park protections.

headline: Tightened rules to cut off wind and solar tax credits
how: Restore the clean-energy tax credit rules.
why: The order tells Treasury and Interior how to enforce existing law, while the credits themselves ended by statute, which needs Congress.

headline: Pushed the start of higher country tariffs back to August 1
why: It delayed tariffs the Supreme Court has since voided, so there is nothing left to undo.

headline: Created a new job category for political hires who push policy inside agencies
why: Schedule G was created by order alone, with no rule behind it, so the order that made it can end it.

headline: Fast-tracked permits for data centers and the power plants that feed them
why: It tells agencies to speed approvals under existing laws, which the same kind of order can reverse.

headline: Made federal AI purchases depend on passing White House ideology tests
why: It sets what AI the federal government will buy; procurement rules are executive policy, not law.

headline: Set up a program to promote exports of U.S. AI systems
why: An export-promotion program under existing trade authority; it picks no winners by law and any president can reshape it.

headline: Pushed homeless people toward forced treatment and cut harm-reduction funding
why: It directs agencies on grant priorities and enforcement and changes no statute, though some local anti-camping laws would stay.

headline: Moved to keep college athletes from being treated as employees
why: It directs the Labor Department and labor board to clarify athlete status, which a later order can redirect; the labor board's own cases decide.

headline: Ended duty-free entry for small imported packages from every country
why: Congress repealed the exemption for 2027 and a court upheld the suspension; a Democratic president would likely keep closing the loophole.

headline: Declared a DC crime emergency and took over the city's police
why: The Home Rule Act limits the takeover to thirty days unless Congress extends it, so the power ended without a pen.

headline: Sped up commercial rocket launch licensing and environmental review
why: A licensing-speed directive to the FAA; both parties want a faster space industry, and environmental law itself is untouched.

headline: Ordered the government to refill its stockpile of key drug ingredients
why: A drug supply-chain reserve that a Democratic president would likely keep.

headline: Scrapped Biden's order pushing agencies to curb corporate monopolies
why: It revoked an earlier order, so a new order can bring its agency competition plans back; no statute is involved.

headline: Created a National Design Studio to redo federal websites and services
why: A design office inside the White House that improves government sites; a Democratic president would keep it.

headline: Created a National Guard unit to police U.S. cities, starting with DC
why: A Defense Department directive under presidential command authority; it creates no statute, so a later order can disband the unit.

headline: Pushed to jail DC arrestees before trial and end cashless bail there
why: It directs federal officers and prosecutors; DC's own bail law is unchanged, so revoking the order ends the federal push.

headline: Ordered prosecutors to go after people who burn the American flag
how: Revoke it and drop the policy.
why: It only directs prosecutors; flag burning remains protected speech under Supreme Court precedent.

headline: Threatened federal funds for states and cities that end cash bail

headline: Stripped union bargaining rights from more federal workers
how: Restore union contracts for those workers.
why: It widens the national-security exclusions of Executive Order 14251 by the same kind of order; courts have mostly let it run.

headline: Made classical style the default for new federal buildings
why: An architecture-style preference for federal buildings with no effect on anyone's rights; a later president can set a different taste.

why: A research-funding push on pediatric cancer data that a Democratic president would keep.
